security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline paths, and relative documentation links. The confirmed risks are the documented Firecrawl connector command and outbound scraping workflow, plus a semantic risk from ingesting untrusted remote page content without an explicit prompt-injection boundary.

remediation.issue: Connector command enables outbound scraping through an external Python script.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running the connector, validate competitor URLs and domains, and document that only public competitor pages should be fetched.

remediation.issue: Fetched competitor pages are converted into LLM-ready markdown without a stated trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Add instructions that scraped page content is untrusted data and that any instructions found in fetched pages must be ignored.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples and relative links trigger noisy static findings.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify examples as non-executable prompts and avoid command-looking inline snippets unless they are required for the workflow.

content.user_title: Analyze Competitor SEO and GEO Strategy
content.value_statement: Teams struggle to compare competitors when keyword, backlink, content, and AI citation signals live in separate tools. This skill structures those inputs into evidence-labeled benchmarks, market gaps, and an action plan.
actual_capabilities: Separates direct competitors, indirect alternatives, and content competitors for a target market.
Structures competitor profiles with traffic, authority, audience, offerings, and business model fields.
Compares keyword rankings, backlink profiles, content strategy, technical SEO, and AI citation signals.
Labels metrics as measured, user-provided, or estimated to reduce unsupported claims.
Produces competitor briefs, comparison tables, battlecards, and immediate to long-term action plans.
limitations: It does not provide live SEO metrics unless the host has tools, exports, or connector access.
Estimated metrics depend on available context and must not be treated as measured data.
It is not the dedicated pairwise topic coverage map for content gaps.
Scraping or connector use may require user approval and must respect site policies.

use_cases.title: Plan an SEO Response
use_cases.description: Compare competitor keywords, content patterns, backlinks, and traffic signals before choosing priority SEO actions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sales Battlecards
use_cases.description: Turn competitor positioning, strengths, weaknesses, pricing notes, and objections into concise battlecard material.

use_cases.title: Find GEO Opportunities
use_cases.description: Review which competitors earn AI citations and identify formats, definitions, or evidence gaps your content can target.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Competitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze SEO and GEO strategy for [competitor URL]. Label each metric as measured, user-provided, or estimated.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competitor Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my site [your URL] with [competitor 1], [competitor 2], and [competitor 3]. Focus on keywords, backlinks, content, and traffic share.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Battlecard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sales and marketing battlecard for [competitor]. Include positioning, strengths, weaknesses, pricing notes, objections, and SEO or GEO signals.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Market Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the competitor set [domains] and our target audience [audience], rank keyword, content, backlink, and AI citation opportunities by impact and evidence quality.

output_examples.input: Analyze why a leading competitor ranks for our core marketing terms.
output_examples.output: A competitor brief with SEO strategy overview, top content patterns, linkable assets, GEO citation factors, weaknesses, and priority opportunities.

output_examples.input: Compare our site with three competitors before a quarterly planning session.
output_examples.output: A comparison table across authority, traffic, top keywords, backlinks, content cadence, AI citations, and a staged action plan.

output_examples.input: Create a battlecard for a competitor our sales team often faces.
output_examples.output: A concise battlecard covering positioning, differentiators, pricing notes, objections, landmine questions, and evidence-backed counterpoints.

best_practices: Provide competitor URLs, your site URL, target market, and any available SEO exports before starting.
Ask the skill to label every metric as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Review the action plan with sales, content, and product teams before assigning owners.
anti_patterns: Do not use stale or unattributed metrics as proof for strategic decisions.
Do not compare only direct competitors when buyers also consider indirect alternatives.
Do not ask for a full content gap map when the dedicated content-gap-analysis skill is a better fit.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your site, 2 to 5 competitor domains, target market, and any SEO, analytics, or sales data you trust.

faq.question: Can it work without paid SEO tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use provided data and estimates, but results should clearly label what is estimated.

faq.question: Does it analyze AI search visibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GEO and AI citation checks, including what competitors are cited for and why.

faq.question: Is this the same as content gap analysis?
faq.answer: No. This skill benchmarks competitors broadly. Use content-gap-analysis for a detailed pairwise topic coverage map.

faq.question: What deliverables can it produce?
faq.answer: It can produce competitor briefs, benchmark tables, battlecards, opportunity lists, and phased action plans.

faq.question: How should estimates be handled?
faq.answer: Treat estimates as directional. Ask for measured labels, source dates, and confidence notes before making decisions.
